name: CHAOS!!! Highway From Hell Tour, Episode #1

date.source: The show script's own dateline ("October 6th, 1996"; the on-air host's own live introduction names the CoreStates Spectrum, Philadelphia); posted in five parts on 21 October 1996.

no_appearances_reason: Roughly twenty named wrestlers across six matches, an eight-member stable, a rotating eight-plus-person broadcast team and an in-fiction president appear across this card; no character records were minted per the depth-is-an-annotation rule and the wciwf-1995/dwo-1996 precedent -- the full roster, matches and results live in the page text.
notes: The fed's own relaunch-era debut broadcast after a summer 1996 shutdown forced by a named rival. Six matches: (1) Anarchy (Maddog and Zombie) defeat the Japanese Dragons (Super White Samurai and Super Blue Ninja), advancing in the CHAOS!!! World Tag Team Championship tournament's winner's bracket; (2) the HammerHeads (Brutus and Bronco Hammersmith) defeat the Powers of Rain (Monsoon and Riptide), also advancing -- the Powers of Rain rename themselves the Wave Runners moments later in the following interview segment; (3) Deranged, a self-billed former three-time WEW International Champion, defeats newcomer G-Dogg; (4) "the Mutilated" Rocco Michaelangelo, debuting, defeats Sabin Rene Figaro with his finisher "the Redemption"; (5) Death Adder defeats Supersonic; (6) the main event, Mr. Deadly defeats the Hollywood Blonde, closing on a backstage/parking-lot brawl between two rival stables, the Evil Empire and the Killer Elite. Between matches, an interview segment introduces the eight-member Storm Guardians stable (Tornado, Windy, Monsoon, Rip Tide, Lightning Dragon, Thunder Dragon, Tempest and Tsunami), who stake a claim on every CHAOS!!! championship in the building. A separate backstage interview introduces newcomer "the Mutilated" Rocco Michaelangelo. The broadcast team's own on-air banter discloses that the fed's president, Mr. NEWZ!!!, was installed to "continue the WEW legacy" after a predecessor promotion ("almost a year" running) folded, and that the fed's own International World Championship was left vacant when "Stunning" Scott Alexander, its prior champion, was stripped of it around the time of this relaunch -- a cross-lane WEW lead, not chased. The tournament's winner's-bracket graphic also names two teams with byes into the next round (Black Rain, described as "former CHAOS!!! World Tag Team Champions," and Apocalypse, described as "former WEW World Tag Team Champions") whose own prior reigns are not otherwise evidenced in the held record and are not structured as reigns here.
